From https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#formatting-commit-messages

"All commit messages must include a "Signed-off-by" line, which indicates that you the contributor have agreed to the Developer Certificate of Origin (see below). This line must include the full name you commonly use, often a given name and a family name or surname. (ok: Sam Samuelsson, Robert A. Heinlein; not ok: xXthorXx, Sam, RAH)"

Please fix your git-config and `git commit --amend --reset-author`. Thanks!
Fixed.
Can you add more “why” here?  What is the design?  Who is the consumer?  Is there a corresponding Redfish profile to use?

In environments where both local and LDAP users are supported, administrators often need to control which authentication method takes precedence.

The GetPAMOrder and SetPAMOrder methods provide a programmatic way to inspect and modify the sequence of PAM modules in /etc/pam.d/common-auth,
allowing administrators to prioritize local (pam_unix.so) or LDAP (pam_ldap.so) authentication without manually editing configuration files.

This is a backend implementation intended to support internal configuration.
The D-Bus methods for GetPAMOrder and SetPAMOrder are not yet mapped to any Redfish interfaces.
We plan to evaluate redfish integration in a future update once the backend changes are reviewed and merged.
What do these bytes represent?  If this is an index of some sort, use size and not byte. Please add documentation.

Bytes represented the pam indices, Modified according to the comment. 
I'll add the document once updated here. https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/architecture/user-management.md
